Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.input:
import os,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
i=G['Demo pair 1 input']; o=G['Demo pair 1 output']
# changed cells
ch=[(r,c,i[r][c],o[r][c]) for r in range(30) for c in range(30) if i[r][c]!=o[r][c]]
print(len(ch), set(v for _,_,_,v in ch))
# which colors change to what
from collections import Counter
print(Counter((a,b) for _,_,a,b in ch))

Better: compute which components get any change and extent.

steps.name: ipython
steps.input:
cs=comps(i)
seeds=[(4,14),(28,17)]
for comp in cs:
    n=sum(1 for y,x in comp if (y,x) in seeds)
    # bounding box
    ys=[y for y,x in comp]; xs=[x for y,x in comp]
    h=max(ys)-min(ys)+1; w=max(xs)-min(xs)+1
    print(len(comp), 'changed:', sum(1 for y,x in comp if o[y][x]!=i[y][x]), 'of',len(comp), 'bbox',h,w)

import os,re,json,itertools
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
from collections import deque
# For each demo: BFS over ALL cells from every seed simultaneously (multi-source, each cell keeps nearest seed color on tie -> tie broken by first arrival); record for each 1-cell: dist & whether changed.
for n in (1,2,3):
    i=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    H,W=len(i),len(i[0])
    seeds=[(y,x,i[y][x]) for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if i[y][x] not in (0,1)]
    dist=[[None]*W for _ in range(H)]; owner=[[None]*W for _ in range(H)]
    q=deque()
    for sy,sx,col in seeds:
        dist[sy][sx]=0; owner[sy][sx]=col; q.append((sy,sx))
    while q:
        y,x=q.popleft()
        for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            yy,xx=y+dy,x+dx
            if 0<=yy<H and 0<=xx<W and dist[yy][xx] is None:
                dist[yy][xx]=dist[y][x]+1; owner[yy][xx]=owner[y][x]; q.append((yy,xx))
    chc={(y,x,o[y][x]) for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if i[y][x]==1 and o[y][x]!=i[y][x]}
    # consistency: changed cell must have owner==new color?
    bad=[c for c in chc if owner[c[0]][c[1]]!=c[2]]
    same=sum(1 for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if i[y][x]==1 and o[y][x]==i[y][x] and owner[y][x] is not None)
    print('demo',n,'changed-with-wrong-owner:',len(bad),'unchanged-reached-by-same-color:',same)
    # also count changed cells whose owner==their new color
    good=sum(1 for y,x,c in chc if owner[y][x]==c)
    print('   changed-correct-owner:',good)

    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
# New idea: maybe recolored region = cells where two DIFFERENT seed colors "cross" along a path... Or maybe: recolored cells lie on the straight lines connecting each pair of seeds (like the segment between them), extended? Let's test collinearity properly with exact integer steps.
from collections import deque
def is_on_line(p,s1,s2):
    dy=s2[0]-s1[0]; dx=s2[1]-s1[1]
    g_=math.gcd(abs(dy),abs(dx)); by,bx=dy//g_,dx//g_
    return (p[0]-s1[0])*bx==(p[1]-s1[1])*by
for n in (1,2,3):
    i_=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; o_=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    HH,WW=len(i_),len(i_[0])
    seeds=[(y,x,i_[y][x]) for y in range(HH) for x in range(WW) if i_[y][x] not in (0,1)]
    ch={(y,x) for y in range(HH) for x in range(WW) if i_[y][x]==1 and o_[y][x]!=i_[y][x]}
    onlines=[]; offlines=[]
    for y,x in ch:
        hit=any(is_on_line((y,x),seeds[j][:2],seeds[k][:2]) for j,k in itertools.combinations(range(len(seeds)),2))
        (onlines if hit else offlines).append((y,x))
    print('demo',n,'changed ON a seed-pair line:',len(onlines),'off:',len(offlines),'total',len(ch))
